text:
I've been working on network protocols, which is super straightforward compared to optimizing the node. I've added support for the handing the `sendaddrv2` message in the version handshake, by adding a derived `protocol_version_70016` and which will be functional once I add derived `protocol_address_in_70016` and `protocol_address_out_70016`. I've also implemented `protocol_header_out_70012`.

Next is `protocol_block_out`, which is very similar to header_out (and I completed the query for it along with the header_out, since they are basically the same). Then just need to add header announcements (`sendheaders` message gets incorporated in `protocol_header_out_70012`) and block announcements in `protocol_block_out` (which is only for blocks-first support).

At that point it's a fully functional blocks-only node, with blocks first and headers first protocol support. We'll want to add the compact filters support (bip157 at protocol level 70015) because we have the store/query available. But there's no reason to implement the compact blocks, mempool, or tx relay protocols until we have a tx pool. Everything else is complete up to bip155 (sendarrdv2, @ network level 70016) and bip340/341/342 (taproot, consensus). I expect all of the above to be complete in a couple of weeks.

text:
I've wrapped up the protocol work. This adds `protocol_block_out_106` , `protocol_block_out_70012` (disables block `inv` announcement when `sendheaders` received), `protocol_header_out_31800` and `protocol_header_out_70012` (enables `headers` announcement when `sendheaders` received).

I also added automatic snapshotting when the node is "recent". This includes new `is_recent()` methods from protocol->session->full_node, a new chaser notification type `chase::recent` , which is posted by confirmation when a just-organized block is at the configured maximum height or the chain is current (based on `is_current()` , which is based on configured time from the top confirmed block timestamp (defaults to 60 minutes). Recency is logged at confirmation chaser startup and if it changed to true.

The `chase::recent` notification is therefore posted 0..1 times for the process. This is caught only by the snapshot chaser, which then takes a snapshot. The snapshot causes all channels to be dropped, the network paused, and restarted when complete. Attachment of protocols to channels tests `is_recent()` when attaching inbound channels, if `delay_inbound` is set in `node.config` , and only attaches block and header inbound protocols when chain is recent. So the recency snapshot serves to reset channels for inbound traffic, and unlike others is not optional/configurable.

I also added duration based events to log the time cost in milliseconds of the snapshot (and a store restart following a disk full resume). Snapshots are typically around a minute. Also added console logging for recency, initial positive state or transition. Finally, added base `session_inbound` connection acceptance disable and verbose logging, with override in node to disable until `is_recent` , also only if `delay_inbound` is configured.

elements.text: On the call today I was trying to remember how the

event is consumed. It is handled by the snapshot chaser, which causes a snapshot to be taken (once the node is "recent" - which means current or max height). A snapshot causes all channels to be dropped, which results in no store activity, which allows the table heads and bodies to be flushed to disk, and the heads copied. This also means that the channels are reopened as "recent" - which results in outbound protocols being attached. This is enforced - not configurable. The node will always snapshot once it is recent.

It is handled by the snapshot chaser, which causes a snapshot to be taken (once the node is "recent" - which means current or max height). A snapshot causes all channels to be dropped, which results in no store activity, which allows the table heads and bodies to be flushed to disk, and the heads copied. elements.text: We don't allow block to be taken in from incoming channels (protocol never attached). We don't attach outbound protocols (txs, blocks|headers) unless the node is recent. Channels have time limits, so don't stay attached perpetually. Recency can regress (e.g. if the node is disconnected) and if it's significant the channels will adapt to the regress as they are connected. The only thing that is sent one time and does not adapt is the

text: We don't allow block to be taken in from incoming channels (protocol never attached). We don't attach outbound protocols (txs, blocks|headers) unless the node is recent. Channels have time limits, so don't stay attached perpetually. Recency can regress (e.g. if the node is disconnected) and if it's significant the channels will adapt to the regress as they are connected. The only thing that is sent one time and does not adapt is the `chase::recent` notification, and that is only used to establish a snapshot, which also resets all channels. We wouldn't want a cycling recency state to cause cycling snapshots. We want just one.
